label: D1 after a reward, with a moderate a2 preference, late in the episode
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never at GO or D2), and only when the reward input is 1 (the previous trial was rewarded). Almost every activation follows an a2 choice (prev_action 2; just 11 of 58779 follow a1), comes before an a2 choice, and occurs when the good state is S2. It is concentrated late in the episode (90% of mass in trials 50-99, almost none before trial 10). 99.8% of activations fall where the model's D1 policy logit(a1)-logit(a2) is in a moderate a2-preferring band [-4.44, -1.52]; it does not fire when a2 preference is saturated (choice < -4.44), when value is high (> 7.7), or after a1. Magnitude is largest on the first reward after an unrewarded or rare streak and decays over consecutive rewards in a run (e.g. 0.45 -> 0.09 -> 0.04). Observed-only alternatives: D1 & reward input & prev_action != 1 & ep_trial >= 50 scores dev F1 0.71 (mass recall 0.90); adding good != 1 (hidden, inferable) gives F1 0.76. The recorded predicate uses the model's own policy logit (dev F1 0.82, mass recall 0.94), so part of the band condition is a readout of the agent's own state, not of the task.

issues: Confirmed core facts: the unit fires only at D1 (0 activations at GO and D2) and only when in_rew==1. Only 11 activations follow a1 and 27 come before an a1 choice. 99.8% of activation mass lies in choice [-4.44,-1.52]. No activations at value >= 8.10, and only 48 in [7.73, 8.10). 89.8% of mass falls in trials 50-99. Reported scores reproduce (dev F1 0.818, test F1 0.814).

Systematic false-positive block: the ep_trial>=40 cutoff is wrong for trials 40-49. Precision there is 0.29 (11477 predicted steps), against 0.85 for ep_trial>=50. Moving the cutoff to 50 alone raises dev F1 to 0.842.

Systematic class the label omits: after a rare-transition rewarded trial (prev_common==0, i.e. a2 -> S1 rare, rewarded) the unit fires well before late episode. In-band precision is 0.80 in trials 10-39 and 0.97 at ep_trial>=40. After common-rewarded trials in trials 20-49 it is only 0.17. So 'late in the episode' is only true for the common-transition case.

'Happens when S2 is the good state' overclaims. 21% of activation mass has good != 2 (7.8% good==1, 13.4% unknown). Within the recorded predicate, precision is actually higher when good==1 (0.80) than when good==2 (0.75).

Magnitude-decay claim is mixed. With prev_action==2, a first reward after an unrewarded trial (tv('reward',-2)==0) fires LESS often (precision 0.385) than a reward continuing a run (0.50 after one prior reward, 0.55 after two). Activations there are larger per active step (mass/recall ratio about 1.34 vs 0.90), but the profile also shows sustained runs of roughly constant magnitude (0.40, 0.40, 0.41, 0.42). Decay is not the general pattern.
Remaining false positives of the recorded predicate are mostly in-band D1 steps inside reward runs and in trials 40-49, not scattered noise.

Observed-only check: D1 & in_rew==1 & prev_action==2 & (ep_trial>=50 | prev_common==0 & ep_trial>=10) scores dev F1 0.70. The policy-logit band stays necessary for the high score, so the explanation still partly reads out the agent's internal policy state.
